explanation: In Tibet the Satluj is called Langchen Khambab ('elephant mouth'); the Indus is Singi Khamban.

exam: APPSC Group-1 PYQ
q: Maihan Dam has been constructed across the River:
explanation: Maithon dam (DVC) is on the Barakar, a tributary of the Damodar.

exam: APPSC AEE (S2) 2023
q: ____ is the site of confluence of the rivers Alaknanda and Pindar.
explanation: Karnaprayag is the confluence of the Alaknanda and the Pindar.

exam: APPSC Divisional Accounts Officer, Assistant Public Relation
q: Which of the following rivers rises in the western Himalayas in the Uttarakhand state of India, and drains into the Sundarbans delta in the Bay of Bengal?
explanation: The Ganga rises in the western Himalayas of Uttarakhand (Gangotri) and drains into the Bay of Bengal through the Sundarbans delta.

notes.text: # Perennial character and work in the plains
- Himalayan rivers show **all three stages** of the erosion cycle (youth, maturity, old age); **Peninsular rivers have reached maturity**.

exam: APPSC Group-I Prelims 2003
q: Which of the following rivers is called 'Padma' in Bangladesh?
explanation: At Farakka the Ganga's right arm, the Padma, enters Bangladesh, so the Padma is the Ganga; the Brahmaputra is the Jamuna there.

notes.text: - In the plains: gentle slope → **meanders, shifting channels, ox-bow lakes, floodplains**, braided channels and riverine islands.

exam: APPSC Forest Section Officer Screening Test General Studies
q: Prayagraj is located at the confluence of .. rivers.
explanation: Prayagraj's Triveni Sangam is the meeting of the Ganga, the Yamuna and the mythical Saraswati.

notes.text: - Marks: **valley-in-valley**, **paired terraces**, **entrenched (ingrown) meanders**.
